title: Knowledge check: Caching Responses and Data

questions.prompt: In Caching Responses and Data, which statement best describes HTTP cache headers?
options: Return the same success response for every request regardless of outcome.
Measure representative traffic first, then optimize the measured bottleneck. Cache only data with an explicit freshness/invalidation policy and bound results and concurrent work.
This option describes a different concept and does not define http cache headers (choice 2).
Move all backend decisions into the browser and trust the submitted values.
questions.answer_key: Measure representative traffic first, then optimize the measured bottleneck. Cache only data with an explicit freshness/invalidation policy and bound results and concurrent work.
questions.explanation: Measure representative traffic first, then optimize the measured bottleneck. Cache only data with an explicit freshness/invalidation policy and bound results and concurrent work.

questions.prompt: Which design rule is most appropriate when applying Caching Responses and Data?
options: Node handles I/O asynchronously, but CPU-heavy work can block the event loop. Measure latency and error rates, limit work, tune data access, control cache freshness, and design backpressure and shutdown behavior.
Trust request fields and skip authorization to keep handlers small.
Suppress all errors without recording safe diagnostic information.
Assume that adding CORS makes private routes authenticated.
questions.answer_key: Node handles I/O asynchronously, but CPU-heavy work can block the event loop. Measure latency and error rates, limit work, tune data access, control cache freshness, and design backpressure and shutdown behavior.
questions.explanation: Node handles I/O asynchronously, but CPU-heavy work can block the event loop. Measure latency and error rates, limit work, tune data access, control cache freshness, and design backpressure and shutdown behavior.

questions.prompt: A change related to Caching Responses and Data appears to work for one normal request. What is the strongest next verification step?
options: Test only one successful request manually and record no expected output.
Use production data to avoid building a small reproducible fixture.
Treat the page’s displayed reference output as proof that Node.js executed the code.
Use repeatable tests for a successful request and at least one invalid/boundary or dependency-failure case.
questions.answer_key: Use repeatable tests for a successful request and at least one invalid/boundary or dependency-failure case.
questions.explanation: Use repeatable tests for a successful request and at least one invalid/boundary or dependency-failure case.
